investigacion.base:
I need week 41 per-prefecture data.I couldn't open the MHLW pages directly. Based on press coverage of the latest MHLW release (week 41), **the answer as of now would be 1 (Okinawa only)**. Okinawa is falling toward 30, though, and no other prefecture is near the threshold yet.

**Latest data (MHLW release of Oct 16, 2026; week 41, Oct 5–11)**
- Nationally: 47,746 cases, up 12.8% from the previous week and about 5.3 times the same week last year (9,074). That works out to 12.81 per sentinel, up from 11.35.
- Top prefectures: Okinawa 31.34 (the highest), then Kanagawa 21.60, Saitama 20.99, Chiba 19.55 and Hokkaido 16.21. Tokyo was 15.88, and 29 prefectures in total were above the advisory level of 10. Okinawa has been above 30 for three straight weeks.
- Okinawa's trend: it peaked at 42.50 in week 39 and has fallen two weeks in a row (42.50 → 37.07 → 31.34). At that pace it would likely drop below 30 in week 42.
- Fast risers: Hokkaido went from 9.21 to 16.21 (+7.00), Iwate +4.75 to 13.34 and Yamaguchi +4.13 to 12.36. Aichi has fallen three weeks running, to 11.47.
- Week 40 for comparison: Kanagawa 18.51, Saitama 19.66, Chiba 18.72, Tokyo 15.87 (1 prefecture at warning level, 15 at advisory level). So the Kanto leaders grew only about 4–17% from week 40 to 41.
- School closures: 1,703 facilities closed in week 41, about 1.82 times the previous week's 937.

**Number of prefectures at warning level (≥30) so far this season:** week 39: 1 (Okinawa); week 40: 1; week 41: 1.

**How the numbers might move**
- To reach 30 by week 43, Kanagawa (21.6) would need about 18% growth per week for two weeks. Saitama would need about 20% and Chiba about 24%. Recent weekly growth in Kanto has been 4–17%, but last season's growth rates show weekly jumps of 30–60% can happen during a takeoff.
- An unusual late-summer surge started in Okinawa and Kanto (week 35 national figure 1.76, at 16 times normal levels). The national curve dipped in week 39 and then rose again.
- Historical comparison: in a typical year, prefectures reach the warning level only around December to February. At peak, dozens of prefectures can be above 30 (for example, in the 2018 season Okinawa hit 54.12 and 33 prefectures had health-centre areas at warning level). In late October, having even one prefecture above 30 is very unusual.

**Scheduled releases**
- About Oct 23: week 42 (Oct 12–18) data. This is the key signal: whether Okinawa stays above 30 and whether Kanagawa, Saitama or Chiba move into the mid-20s.
- About Oct 30: week 43 data, which decides the question.

**Status quo:** 1, but likely to fall to 0 if Okinawa keeps declining. The realistic range looks like 0–2, with some upside risk if growth in Kanto picks up again.

I didn't find any prediction-market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves as the number of Japan's 47 prefectures whose average reported influenza cases per sentinel medical institution ("定点当たり報告数") is 30.00 or greater for the surveillance week of October 19–25, 2026 (2026 week 43), as reported in Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) weekly influenza status release ("インフルエンザの発生状況について"), expected to be published on or about October 30, 2026. The list of weekly press releases is available at https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou01/houdou_00023.html and per-prefecture figures at https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/houkokusuunosuii_00007.html . The warning level ("警報") threshold is 30 cases per sentinel institution. For example, if exactly 8 prefectures report a per-sentinel average of 30.00 or higher that week, this resolves as 8.
letra_pequena: The count is based on the per-prefecture average cases per sentinel medical institution for the designated surveillance week only (not cumulative or national figures). If the MHLW figures are not published in time, the same per-prefecture weekly values as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) (e.g. Jiji Press / Nippon.com weekly flu coverage) will be used. If MHLW revises the figures, the most recent published values for that surveillance week govern. If the per-prefecture weekly data is never published anywhere, the question is annulled.

**(a) Time until the outcome is known:** About 11 days. The week-43 report (Oct 19–25) is due around Oct 30, 2026. The week-42 report, due around Oct 23, will be a strong intermediate signal.

**(b) Outcome if nothing changed:** 1. Okinawa is the only prefecture at or above 30 (31.34 in week 41).

**(c) Outcome if the current trend continued:**
- **Okinawa:** it is falling about 15% per week (42.5 → 37.1 → 31.3). At that pace it would be roughly 26–27 in week 42 and 22–23 in week 43, so it likely drops out.
- **Kanto leaders:** Kanagawa (21.6), Saitama (21.0) and Chiba (19.6) have been growing 4–17% per week. At 15% growth, Kanagawa reaches about 28.6 in week 43, just short of 30.
- **Hokkaido:** it rose 76% in one week, to 16.21. At about 40% per week it would reach roughly 31–32 in week 43.
- **Holiday effect:** week 42 contains Sports Day (Oct 12), which may depress reports that week, followed by a rebound in week 43.

Trend extrapolation therefore gives roughly 0–2 prefectures. If takeoff growth accelerates to 30–50% per week, as in last season's November surge, it could be 3–6 or more.

**(d) Experts and markets:** No prediction markets were found. Seasonal surveillance commentary sees activity rising nationally (12.8% week on week, about 5 times last year's level). However, in a typical year the warning level is not reached until December or later, so several prefectures above 30 in October would be historically unusual.

**(e) Low-outcome scenario:** Okinawa keeps declining and Kanto growth stalls around 20–25. The holiday-affected week 42 shows a plateau, and growth stays modest in week 43. Result: 0.

**(f) High-outcome scenario:** A shift in the dominant strain or a school-driven takeoff produces 40–60% weekly growth across Kanto, Hokkaido and Tohoku. Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba, Tokyo, Hokkaido and possibly Miyagi or Iwate all cross 30, and Okinawa rebounds. Result: 6–10 or more.

Overall I put about 40% on 0 prefectures, about 25% on 1, about 15% on 2, about 10% on 3–4 and about 10% on 5 or more. That gives a median near 1 with a right-skewed tail.
